mise_stderr mktemp (line 110) has no signal trap; a Ctrl-C during mise where's network call leaves one empty $TMPDIR/tmp.* file. Every normal path removes it before fail. Not requested.
Header comment line 93-94 reads `before NATS and the listener are already up` (`are up`). Wording; batched into the fast-follow.

Fake mise's two failure knobs (SMOKE_MISE_WHERE_FAILS, SMOKE_MISE_CONFIG_ERROR) could be one text knob; sed pin (line 25) reports sed's own error rather than the fixture message on a checkout path containing `|` (not a path this rig can have; grep -Fxq guard covers `&`). Not requested.

Five bare-directory checkpoint invocations (lines 476-570) repeat a seven-line env prefix; run_checkpoint (line 162) hard-binds SMOKE_DIR. Named as the single Fast-follow: parametrize run_checkpoint on the smoke directory; up.sh comment wording rides along.
